title: He found the genetic switch behind the most common prostate cancer mutation. It just won him medicine's Harrington Prize.

sources.text: Michigan Medicine - International Harrington Prize Jointly Awarded to Drs. Arul Chinnaiyan and Charles Sawyers
BioPatrika - Arul Chinnaiyan Wins 2026 Harrington Prize for Breakthrough Prostate Cancer Research

caption:
He found the genetic switch behind the most common prostate cancer mutation. It just won him medicine's Harrington Prize.

A second-generation Indian-American and Howard Hughes Medical Institute Investigator at the University of Michigan, Chinnaiyan discovered the TMPRSS2-ERG gene fusion - the most common genetic alteration found in prostate cancer.

His research into mutations that respond to PARP inhibitors like olaparib turned a one-size-fits-all disease into one doctors could increasingly treat based on a patient's specific genetics - precision medicine instead of guesswork.

Chinnaiyan's discovery didn't just explain prostate cancer - it became the first University of Michigan work to win this particular prize, built on exactly the kind of mechanism-first science precision medicine depends on.
